deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This page belongs to Riemann's work on the self-gravitating homogeneous fluid ellipsoid (Dirichlet's problem). That work became the paper 'Ein Beitrag zu den Untersuchungen über die Bewegung eines gleichartigen flüssigen Ellipsoides' (Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 9, 1861). The previous page sets up the kinematics. The axes ξ,η,ζ rotate with the body. Two families of angular velocities appear, (p,q,r) or (u,v,w) and (p1,q1,r1) or (u',v',w'). The semi-axes a,b,c depend on t. This page holds algebraic side calculations for steady configurations in which both rotation vectors lie in one principal plane: u = u' = 0, so only v,w,v',w' survive and a is the axis normal to that plane.

A. An algebraic condition on the axes.
(1) Riemann expands D = (a+c)^4((2a-c)^2-b^2) - (a-c)^4((2a+c)^2-b^2).
(2) He splits off the b^2-part. Since (a+c)^4-(a-c)^4 = 8ac(a^2+c^2), this part is -b^2·2(a^2+c^2)·4ac.
(3) The rest is a difference of squares, X^2 - Y^2, with X = (a+c)^2(2a-c) and Y = (a-c)^2(2a+c).
(4) He computes X explicitly: X = 2a^3+4a^2c+2ac^2 - a^2c - 2ac^2 + c^3 = 2a^3+3a^2c-c^3. By symmetry (my step) Y = 2a^3-3a^2c+c^3.
(5) Hence X+Y = 4a^3 and X-Y = 2c(3a^2-c^2). This gives D = 8ac[a^2(3a^2-c^2) - b^2(a^2+c^2)].
(6) So D = 0 exactly when b^2 = a^2(3a^2-c^2)/(a^2+c^2). He writes this formula separately.
(7) Clearing denominators, this is equivalent to f(a) := 3a^4 - a^2(b^2+c^2) - b^2c^2 = 0. This f is the expression written next to the stain.

B. Locating the root.
(1) He tests the endpoints, assuming b > c. At a = c: f = 2c^4-2b^2c^2 = 2c^2(c^2-b^2) < 0. At a = b: f = 2b^2(b^2-c^2) > 0. So a root lies with c < a < b.
(2) This is consistent with his marginal notes. From b^2 = a^2(3a^2-c^2)/(a^2+c^2): b^2 > a^2 iff 3a^2-c^2 > a^2+c^2 iff a > c. Also b^2 > c^2 iff (3a^2+c^2)(a^2-c^2) > 0.
(3) He records the decomposition f(a) = 2c^2(c^2-b^2) + (a^2-c^2)(3a^2+2c^2-b^2), i.e. f(a) - f(c) factored by (a^2-c^2).
(4) A side identity: -a^4-b^2c^2+2a^2bc = -(a^2-bc)^2. This equals -((b-c)/2)^4 when a = (b+c)/2, apparently a trial value of a.
(5) He solves the quadratic in a^2. Multiplying f by 12: 36a^4-12a^2(b^2+c^2)-12b^2c^2 = (6a^2-b^2-c^2)^2 - (b^2+c^2)^2 - 12b^2c^2.
(6) The positive root is a^2 = [b^2+c^2+sqrt((b^2+c^2)^2+12b^2c^2)]/6.

C. Steady-state conditions with rotations in a principal plane.
(1) Two bilinear conditions:
 E1: (b-a)vw + (c-a)vw + (b+a)v'w' + (c+a)v'w' = 0, i.e. (b+c-2a)vw + (b+c+2a)v'w' = 0.
 E2: (a+b)vw' + (a-c)vw' + (b-a)v'w - (a+c)v'w = 0, i.e. (b-c+2a)vw' + (b-c-2a)v'w = 0.
(2) A first elimination attempt adds E1 and E2. It groups the b-terms as ((a+b)w'+(b-a)w)(v+v'), against c-terms proportional to (w-w'). It is left unfinished, marked '(v'-v)'.
(3) He then multiplies E1 by (b-c) and E2 by (b+c), as the marginal 'b+c' indicates. This turns every coefficient into a difference of squares:
 E1': ((b-a)^2-(c-a)^2)vw + ((a+b)^2-(a+c)^2)v'w' = 0
 E2': ((b+a)^2-(c-a)^2)vw' + ((b-a)^2-(a+c)^2)v'w = 0.
(4) Subtracting, E1' - E2', separates the b-part from the c-part:
 (v-v')((a-b)^2 w - (a+b)^2 w') = (w-w')((a-c)^2 v - (a+c)^2 v').

D. Time-dependent equations (middle left).
(1) He writes a component of the equations of motion in the rotating frame:
 ∂(a r1 - b r)/∂t + (∂a/∂t) r1 - r ∂b/∂t - p1(cq - a q1) + q(bp - c p1) + bpq + a p1 q1 - 2c p1 q.
(2) He specialises to p1 = q1 = r1 = 0, i.e. no internal vorticity relative to the frame, and writes:
 -∂(br)/∂t - r ∂b/∂t + bpq = 0
 ∂(ar)/∂t + r ∂a/∂t + apq = 0.
(3) These are of the form (1/b) d(b^2 r)/dt = bpq, i.e. angular-momentum / circulation balances.

E. Upside-down block (bottom).
It holds linear relations among products of the axes and rotation components, e.g. c r' = c q - b q' (reading uncertain). It also has a formula for ∂(ξ/a)/∂t. These continue the kinematics of the previous page; they are too illegible to reconstruct reliably.
errors: Line 3 writes '- b(a^2+c^2)' inside the bracket; it must be b^2(a^2+c^2). The preceding term -b^2·2(a^2+c^2)·4ac and the later formula b^2 = a^2(3a^2-c^2)/(a^2+c^2) show this is a slip of the pen.
Line 1 omits a bracket: the second term should be (a-c)^4((2a+c)^2-b^2), as the next line -b^2((a+c)^4-(a-c)^4) shows.

The first elimination attempt (sum E1+E2) appears to contain a sign or double-counting slip. The correct form is ((a+b)w'+(b-a)w)(v+v') = ((a+c)v'+(a-c)v)(w-w'). Riemann has (w'-w) on the right, with an extra (c-a)v(w-w') written above. He abandoned this line for the cleaner difference-of-squares route, which is correct.

In the p1=q1=r1=0 specialisation, the displayed general expression would give q·bp + bpq = 2bpq, but Riemann writes bpq. Either the line '+bpq+ap1q1-2cp1q' is a separate correction, or there is a slip. This cannot be decided from the page (uncertain).
Written '-(a^2-bc)^2 = -((b-c)/2)^4' holds only at a = (b+c)/2, not identically. This is presumably a trial substitution, not an error.

results.what: Factorisation (a+c)^4((2a-c)^2-b^2)-(a-c)^4((2a+c)^2-b^2) = 8ac[a^2(3a^2-c^2)-b^2(a^2+c^2)], giving the axis relation 3a^4 - a^2(b^2+c^2) - b^2c^2 = 0, equivalently b^2 = a^2(3a^2-c^2)/(a^2+c^2), with root in c<a<b and explicit a^2 = (b^2+c^2+sqrt((b^2+c^2)^2+12b^2c^2))/6
results.modern_name: boundary/locus condition in the (a,b,c) axis-ratio plane for Riemann ellipsoids with rotation and vorticity vectors in a principal plane (types II/III in Chandrasekhar's terminology)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1861 (existence domains of Riemann ellipsoids); systematised by Chandrasekhar (1965-69, Ellipsoidal Figures of Equilibrium)

results.what: Reduction of the steady-state equations with u=u'=0 to (v-v')((a-b)^2w-(a+b)^2w') = (w-w')((a-c)^2v-(a+c)^2v'), by multiplying by (b-c) and (b+c) and subtracting
results.modern_name: equilibrium conditions for Riemann ellipsoids with non-aligned rotation and vorticity in a principal plane

results.what: Rotating-frame equations of motion with internal rotation set to zero: d(br)/dt + r db/dt = bpq, d(ar)/dt + r da/dt = -apq
results.modern_name: Dirichlet-Dedekind-Riemann ellipsoid dynamics (virial / angular momentum and circulation equations)

deep.surprise_reason: These are working calculations toward Riemann's published 1861 ellipsoid paper. They cover the steady configurations with rotation axes in a principal plane and the algebraic condition delimiting them. The algebra is elementary and the physics is already attributed to him; at most this is a minor unpublished intermediate.

transcription_corrections: Line 3: '8ac(a^2(3a^2-c^2)-b(a^2+c^2))' — the manuscript is read as 'b' but the content requires b^2.
The line '(a+c)^2(2a-c)=(a^2+2ac+c^2)' continues with the factor (2a-c) multiplied out on the next lines. In '-a^2c-2 +c^3' the '-2' abbreviates -2ac^2.
'c^2 = 3a^4 - a^2(b^2+c^2) - b^2c^2' is better read as a free-standing expression f = 3a^4 - a^2(b^2+c^2) - b^2c^2, with 'b>c' as the marginal hypothesis. The leading 'c^2 =' is doubtful.
'2a^4-2b^2c^2=2c^2(c^2-b^2)<0' is the value of f at a=c (i.e. 2c^4-2b^2c^2).
'b^2>c^2' and '3a^2-c^2>a^2+c^2' are marginal inequalities attached to b^2 = a^2(3a^2-c^2)/(a^2+c^2), not to the vw-equation.
The 'b+c' before '(b-c+2a)vw'+(b-c-2a)v'w' is a multiplier annotation (the equation is multiplied by b+c), not part of the formula.
'(b-a)+c-a' is a note that (b-a)+(c-a)=b+c-2a, linking the two forms of E1.
The bottom block is written upside down and is largely illegible; the listed relations (c r' = c q - b q' etc.) are conjectural.
